docs.speaker: ECB Governing Council — statement
docs.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A) — Statement
docs.quote: We will follow a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach to determining the appropriate monetary policy stance. … More volatile and risk-averse financial markets, together with higher long-term interest rates, could weigh on demand and thereby lower inflation as well.

docs.speaker: ECB Governing Council — press conference Q&A
docs.title: Monetary policy statement (with Q&A) — Q&A
docs.quote: So energy prices have increased inflation, long-term financing costs have qualified the magnitude of that increase, and it's in those circumstances – which we will be very attentive to in the weeks to come, and with another special focus on underlying inflation – that we will make our decision in December. … I would like to know if this no-hiking thing, because of tighter financial conditions in the markets, is one thing only for this meeting, or if it will happen to continue throughout November, the ECB could not hike or keep interest rates unchanged again because of that?

docs.speaker: Isabel Schnabel
docs.title: Navigating stormy waters: reflections on monetary policy
docs.quote: [ 1 ] We have moved from a world in which inflation was persistently too low to one marked by recurrent inflationary shocks; from a historically accommodative monetary policy stance to the fastest tightening cycle in the history of the ECB; and from a deeply integrated global economy to one increasingly shaped by fragmentation and geopolitical tensions. … Policy rates can be adjusted swiftly at each meeting, whereas large-scale asset purchases continue to provide monetary accommodation long after the purchases themselves have ended (Slide 6, right-hand side).

docs.speaker: Christine Lagarde
docs.title: Interview with Yomiuri Shimbun
docs.quote: Long-term interest rates are also higher. … So, learning from this, do you think there is a need for an interest rate hike before any secondary effects become apparent?

docs.speaker: Joachim Nagel
docs.title: “Turn the interest rate screw”
docs.quote: “Turn the interest rate screw” Interview with tagesschau.de The Interview was conducted by Steffen Clement from Hessischer Rundfunk for “plusminus”, a business programme on German TV. … Possibly, we’ll have to act again on that front and turn the interest rate screw.

docs.speaker: Boris Vujčić
docs.title: Resilience in an age of shocks: lessons from central and eastern Europe
docs.quote: When we look at fiscal flows, budget deficits have increased across much of the region in recent years, reflecting a combination of higher social and investment spending, rising public sector wage bills, higher interest rate expenditure and, increasingly, greater defence spending. … [ 10 ] At the same time, geopolitical tensions can disrupt key trade routes and increase the costs and uncertainty associated with complex global value chains.

docs.speaker: ECB Governing Council — account
docs.title: Account: Meeting of 28-29 October 2026
docs.quote: Euro area risk-free rates had stabilised and, at longer tenors, had even declined since the September meeting, while US rates had risen across maturities on the back of higher real rates. … On the one hand, high current inflation and elevated short‑term inflation expectations were seen as implying lower real interest rates at shorter maturities and a more accommodative policy stance than nominal rates alone would suggest, despite the tightening in overall financial conditions.
